description.short: Smooth, balanced black tea from a historic transit corridor in the western hills of Sri Lanka
description.overview: A lesser-known yet historic tea-producing region nestled in the verdant foothills between the coastal plains and high mountains.
description.taste: Soft, harmonious flavor free of aggressive bite or heavy astringency
description.processing: Plucking → withering → orthodox rolling → full oxidation → drying

history.origin: Situated along the natural trade routes connecting coastal Colombo with the high kingdom of Kandy, Kegalle emerged as a key logistical and processing center.
history.development: Estates flourished alongside rubber and spice plantations, cultivating balanced teas valued for their steady character.
history.modern: Today Kegalle teas are primarily integrated into balanced commercial blends, celebrated for reliable quality and approachable flavor.
interestingFacts: Kegalle is widely renowned for the Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage, one of the island's most celebrated conservation sanctuaries, occasionally eclipsing its tea reputation.
